pr.title: perf(cake_sage): cut host time per call and recover GB300 GPU-bound latency of the FP8 block-sparse attention
pr.body:
This PR speeds up Sage FP8 block-sparse attention. The kernel runs on FP8 E4M3 Q/K/V. It uses per-token Q scales, per-16-token K scales, per-channel V scales and block-sparse KV selection. It comes in three forms:
- pre-quantized FP8 attention;
- the combined API, which runs a fused BF16 quantizer and then the attention;
- an INT8-QK/FP8-PV variant for sm_120a.

This PR changes the pre-quantized and combined forms on sm_100a and sm_103a. It changes the attention launch and route choice. The attention entries now take float8_e4m3fn Q/K/V directly. The wrapper no longer makes uint8 views on every call. It allocates the output like Q and launches the entry directly. Both changes lower the host (CPU) cost of each call. On sm_103a, the fused BF16 quantizer in the combined API now lets the attention launch start right after the quantizer starts, not after its last store. This uses programmatic dependent launch (PDL). Because of this, the sm_103a tail-split attention route now launches with PDL on every row, with no exception for small rows.

Main is FlashInfer main 42bbaf163d, which this branch has merged and which is still the previous Cake version. Outputs are bit-identical to main. Compared with main, the pre-quantized attention call takes 1.859-1.947x less host time on B200 and 1.968-2.067x less on GB300 across the 15-row shape list. For example, GB300 B8/H32/Hkv32/S4096 sel 6 goes from 41.09 to 20.05 µs. The combined API call takes 1.380-1.497x less host time on B200 and 1.366-1.425x less on GB300. This matters for small calls whose latency is set by the CPU. On GB300, the combined call was also measured queued behind other GPU work (GPU-bound). This PR is faster on GPU-bound rows that use the sm_103a tail-split route. These rows come from a wider shape grid than the tables. Each row below shows main µs → PR µs, then the speedup:
- B1/H3/Hkv3/S4096 sel 24: 33.22 → 28.88, 1.150
- B1/H5/Hkv5/Sq=Sk=2048 sel 24: 29.13 → 25.08, 1.161
- B1/H5/Hkv5/S4096 sel 24: 37.49 → 33.38, 1.123
- B1/H10/Hkv10/Sq=Sk=2048 sel 24: 35.08 → 31.22, 1.124

Speedup is main / PR, so a value above 1 means this PR is faster. Each run takes the median over 16 paired rounds. Each latency is the median of 4 runs: 2 GPUs, each with a fixed and a rotated shape order. The table columns mean:
- graph: the combined API under CUDA graph (CUPTI GPU time, cold L2).
- GPU-bound: the eager combined call queued behind a spin kernel (CUDA events).
- eager: the eager combined call (CUPTI).
- Host time: the wall clock of the Python call.

Shapes are B/H/Hkv/S with Sq = Sk. sel is the number of selected KV blocks per row. † marks a row whose attention launch in the combined call differs from main. On sm_103a every combined call also starts the attention launch early behind the quantizer; that alone is not marked by †. A row counts as slower only if both of these hold:
- its median paired ratio exceeds 1 by more than run-to-run noise;
- this PR is slower in at least 14 of 16 rounds.

By that rule, no row in the GPU tables is slower than main on either GPU. The lowest cells are 0.993 (B200 GPU-bound, B8/H32/Hkv32/S4096 sel 58) and 0.995 (GB300 GPU-bound, B2/H24/Hkv24/S16384 sel 32). Neither meets the rule. The highest cells are 1.059 (GB300 eager, B1/H8/Hkv8/S4096 sel 6), 1.047 (GB300 GPU-bound, B1/H8/Hkv8/S4096 sel 6) and 1.030 (B200 graph, B1/H8/Hkv8/S4096 sel 32 †).

+    """Run ``call`` on ``stream`` after the stream sleeps and then rewrites ``inputs``

+        assert str(info.value).startswith(message[:-3]), str(info.value)

+    """Every refusal of a pre-quantized call: the exception type and full message, the
+    first failing check when a call has several faults, ``None`` from the dispatcher's
+    fallback and the same refusal through ``bsa_attn_sm100_blk64_fwd(backend="cake")``."""
+    from flashinfer.cute_dsl.sparse.bsa_attn_sm100_blk64 import bsa_attn_sm100_blk64_fwd
+
+    q8, k8, v8, q_scale, k_scale, v_scale, index = _inputs(2, 4, 2, 128, 256, 2, 11)
+    valid = dict(
+        q=q8,
+        k=k8,
+        v=v8,
+        q2k_block_index=index,
+        block_sparse_num=2,
+        q_scale=q_scale,
+        k_scale=k_scale,
+        v_scale=v_scale,
+    )
+    out, _ = bsa_attn_sm100_sage_fwd_cake(**valid)
+    assert out.shape == (2, 128, 4, _HEAD_DIM) and out.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    assert out.is_contiguous() and out.device == q8.device
+    dispatch = backend.sm100_sage_fwd_cake_dispatch

+        ops = {**valid, **replaced}
+        _raises(exc, message, bsa_attn_sm100_sage_fwd_cake, **ops)
+        _raises(exc, message, dispatch, **ops)
+        assert dispatch(**ops, fallback=True) is None, case
+        # The dispatcher reads Q/K/V shapes and requires the three scales itself first.
+        if all(isinstance(ops[name], torch.Tensor) for name in ("q", "k", "v")) and (
+            ops["q_scale"] is not None
+        ):
+            _raises(exc, message, bsa_attn_sm100_blk64_fwd, **ops, backend="cake")
+    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
+

+class _Scale(float):
+    """A float subclass (a caller's own scale type)."""
+
+
+def test_attention_accepts_scales_and_allocates_contiguous_outputs() -> None:
+    """Every accepted ``softmax_scale`` form gives the bits of its float value, and each
+    entry allocates its outputs as contiguous BF16 / float32 tensors on the inputs'
+    device, also for Q whose size-1 dimensions carry other strides."""
+    from flashinfer.cute_dsl.sparse.bsa_attn_sm100_blk64 import bsa_attn_sm100_blk64_fwd
+
+    q8, k8, v8, q_scale, k_scale, v_scale, index = _inputs(1, 1, 1, 128, 256, 2, 13)
+    scales = dict(q_scale=q_scale, k_scale=k_scale, v_scale=v_scale)
+    ref, _ = bsa_attn_sm100_sage_fwd_cake(q8, k8, v8, index, 2, **scales)

+    for scale in (default, _Scale(default), None):
+        out, _ = bsa_attn_sm100_sage_fwd_cake(
+            q8, k8, v8, index, 2, softmax_scale=scale, **scales

+        assert torch.equal(out, ref), scale

+        q8, k8, v8, index, 2, softmax_scale=1, **scales
+    )
+    assert out_one.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and not torch.equal(out_one, ref)
+    # Q of shape (1, 128, 1, 128) as a transposed (1, 1, 128, 128) buffer: contiguous,
+    # strides of its size-1 dimensions differ from a fresh tensor's.
+    q_odd = torch.empty((1, 1, 128, _HEAD_DIM), dtype=q8.dtype, device=q8.device)
+    q_odd = q_odd.transpose(1, 2)
+    q_odd.copy_(q8)
+    assert q_odd.is_contiguous() and q_odd.stride() != q8.stride()
+    q_bf16 = torch.randn((1, 128, 1, _HEAD_DIM), device=q8.device).bfloat16()
+    k_bf16 = torch.randn((1, 256, 1, _HEAD_DIM), device=q8.device).bfloat16()
+    calls = {
+        "attention": lambda q: bsa_attn_sm100_sage_fwd_cake(
+            q, k8, v8, index, 2, return_lse=True, **scales
+        ),
+        "dispatch": lambda q: backend.sm100_sage_fwd_cake_dispatch(
+            q, k8, v8, index, 2, return_lse=True, **scales
+        ),
+        "dispatch_fallback": lambda q: backend.sm100_sage_fwd_cake_dispatch(
+            q, k8, v8, index, 2, return_lse=True, fallback=True, **scales
+        ),
+        "sglang": lambda q: bsa_attn_sm100_blk64_fwd(
+            q, k8, v8, index, 2, return_lse=True, **scales
+        ),
+        "combined": lambda q: backend.bsa_attn_sm100_sage_quantize_fwd_cake(
+            q_bf16, k_bf16, k_bf16, index, 2, return_lse=True
+        ),
+    }
+    for name, call in calls.items():
+        for q in (q8, q_odd):
+            out, lse = call(q)
+            assert type(out) is torch.Tensor and type(lse) is torch.Tensor, name
+            assert out.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and lse.dtype == torch.float32, name
+            assert out.shape == (1, 128, 1, _HEAD_DIM), name
+            assert out.stride() == (128 * _HEAD_DIM, _HEAD_DIM, _HEAD_DIM, 1), name
+            assert lse.shape == (1, 1, 128) and lse.stride() == (128, 128, 1), name
+            assert out.device == q8.device and lse.device == q8.device, name
+            if name != "combined":
+                assert torch.equal(out, ref), name
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
